findings.claim: Before this change, one embedder request held at most 8 texts (the `embed` --limit), each capped at 1,500 runes. Now index() and EmbedPending send every chunk of every selected memory in a single Embed call. maxChunks defaults to 0 (no cap), SetMaxChunks is called only from a test, and no body size limit exists. So one request can hold 8 x ceil(len/1500) texts, about 88 for the store's longest body of 16,277 characters and more for larger bodies. The Ollama client has a fixed 60 s HTTP timeout (internal/embed/ollama.go:34), and the help text of the cli `embed --limit` flag already warns 'large notes time out in bigger batches' (internal/cli/cli.go:266). If a batch times out, EmbedPending returns 0 with an error and stores nothing. It always picks the same first pending memories (`order by m.id limit ?`), so rerunning `embed` fails on the same batch, and every later memory, including memories that have no chunk 0 at all, never gets embedded. Lowering --limit to 1 does not help once a single memory's chunks exceed the timeout. On save, the same failure means a long memory no longer gets even the chunk-0 vector it always got before. Its save returns only an 'embedding pending' warning and it drops out of dense search. This puts at risk the S3 in-place upgrade through `memorycard embed` on the live store (about 7,100 extra chunks on CPU, per L1).
